ears: WHEN, on Linux, the total is N and N heavy jobs in any mix of bridge compiles and wrapper test runs hold slots THE SYSTEM SHALL make the next compile or test run wait. (M1)
WHEN, on Linux, a slot frees while both a compile and a test run are waiting THE SYSTEM SHALL let a waiter take it, whichever kind it is, so each kind can use every slot of the total. (M1)

IF, on Linux, a slot holder of either kind is killed with SIGKILL THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL let the next caller of either kind take that slot without manual cleanup and without waiting for a stale age. (M2)
WHEN, on Linux, only `AL_BRIDGE_MAX_PARALLEL_ALC` is set to N THE SYSTEM SHALL cap bridge compiles and wrapper test runs together at N. (M3)
WHEN, on Linux, no budget setting is set THE SYSTEM SHALL cap bridge compiles and wrapper test runs together at 2. (M3)
WHEN `AL_RUNNER_SLOTS` is set THE SYSTEM SHALL leave the total unchanged and print one stderr line naming the setting that governs it. (M4)
WHEN a bridge compile or a wrapper test run has to wait for a slot THE SYSTEM SHALL emit a progress notice when the wait starts and at least every 15 s until it ends. (M5)
IF a bridge compile's wait for a slot times out THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return a BUSY result carrying no compile diagnostics. (M6)
IF a wrapper test run's wait for a slot times out THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL exit 75 with a BUSY line on stderr and not start the runner. (M6)
IF, on Linux, the bridge and the wrapper are configured with different totals A < B THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL never hold more than B slots at once. (N2)
IF the bridge or the wrapper cannot enforce the shared cap THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL report that in the bridge's compile output / the wrapper's stderr rather than run silently uncapped. (N3)
WHEN the bridge runs on Windows THE SYSTEM SHALL keep capping concurrent alc runs at `AL_BRIDGE_MAX_PARALLEL_ALC` as today. (N1)
WHEN the wrapper is called in a mode that takes no slot today THE SYSTEM SHALL start the runner at once even with every slot taken. (N4)
